newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman on Tyco /Keystone.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman on Tyco /Keystone.

text.p: Lehman Brothers analyst Phua Young said he raised his 18-month target price on Tyco International Ltd shares $100 from "at least $75" after Tyco announced an agreement to acquire valve-maker Keystone International Inc for about $1.2 billion in stock.

-- "It is another typical Tyco deal, very opportunistic. They have had an eye on Keystone for four or five years. The company has not done well; profits have been under pressure. Tyco is paying a big price for what we know today, but there is a lot of earnings potential to come. It is accretive like all of Tyco's deals and we like it," the analyst said.

-- Young said Tyco may have waited until now to acquire Keyston for two reasons. First, "Keystone had a change in mangement two years ago and maybe Tyco wanted to see if they could turn the ship around."
-- Second, he said Tyco has enjoyed a recent climb in stock price, making its shares a more valuable currency for acqusitions.

-- When asked if the Tyco management could become overburdened by a series of large takeovers in recent months, the analyst said, "It is a fear, but this is another business within Tyco that Keystone is going into. The other acquisitions are going into the other parts of the company. If they were to make another big one in one of the four segments, they may be maxing out."

-- Tyco is an industrial and consumer products company with operation in fire and safety services, flow control products, electrical and electronic components and disposable and specialty products. 1996 revenues were $5.1 billion and net earnings were $310.1 million, or $2.03 per share.
-- The companies said overnight Keystone holders will get 0.54183 Tyco shares for each Keystone share, subject to adjustment based on the trading value of Tyco stock.
-- Based on Tyco's Tuesday closing price of $62.75, the terms valued Keystone, a maker of valves and other flow-control equipment, at $34 per share, or $1.2 billion.
-- Tyco shares were off 1-1/8 to 61-5/8, putting the value of Keystone's shares in the deal at about $33.40.
